title: Open question on $R_\ell(K_{1,2}, k)$ for odd $k$
statement_text: We do not know whether $R_\ell(K_{1,2}, k)$ is $k + 1$ or $k + 2$ when $k$ is odd.
context_text: The $k$-colour list Ramsey number $R_\ell(G,k)$ of a graph $G$ (the subscript $\ell$ stands for "list") is the minimum $n$ such that there is an assignment $L$ of lists of $k$ colours (subsets of $\mathbb{N}$ of size $k$) to the edges of $K_n$ such that every $L$-colouring of $E(K_n)$ (each edge receives a colour from its own list) contains a monochromatic copy of $G$; $R(G,k)$ is the ordinary $k$-colour Ramsey number, obtained when all lists are equal, so $R_\ell(G,k)\le R(G,k)$. An edge-colouring has no monochromatic $K_{1,2}$ if and only if it is proper, so $R(K_{1,2},k)$ (resp. $R_\ell(K_{1,2},k)$) is the smallest $n$ with $\chi'(K_n)>k$ (resp. $\chi'_\ell(K_n)>k$), where $\chi'_\ell$ is the list chromatic index (the list chromatic number of the line graph). Häggkvist and Janssen proved $\chi'_\ell(K_n)\le n$ for every $n$, so $\chi'_\ell(K_n)=\chi'(K_n)$ for odd $n$; this gives $R_\ell(K_{1,2},k)=k+1=R(K_{1,2},k)$ when $k$ is even. For odd $k$, $R(K_{1,2},k)=k+2$, and deciding whether $R_\ell(K_{1,2},k)$ equals $k+1$ or $k+2$ amounts to deciding whether $\chi'_\ell(K_{k+1})=k+1$ or $k$, i.e. the List Colouring Conjecture ($\chi'_\ell=\chi'$) for cliques of even order $k+1$, which is open. The authors conjecture more generally that $R_\ell(K_{1,r},k)=R(K_{1,r},k)$ for all $r,k$; they prove the two differ by at most one and are equal for two colours or for $r$ large compared to $k$.
notes: Stated in prose; directly tied to the open case of the List Colouring Conjecture for cliques of even order.

title: Open problem on equality $R_\ell(K_r, 2) = R(K_r, 2)$ for $r > 3$
statement_text: For $r > 3$ we cannot even decide the equality of the two Ramsey numbers $R_\ell(K_r,2)$ (list Ramsey number) and $R(K_r,2)$ (ordinary Ramsey number) of $K_r$ when $k = 2$.
context_text: The $k$-colour list Ramsey number $R_\ell(G,k)$ of a graph $G$ (the subscript $\ell$ stands for "list") is the minimum $n$ such that there is an assignment $L$ of lists of $k$ colours (subsets of $\mathbb{N}$ of size $k$) to the edges of $K_n$ such that every $L$-colouring of $E(K_n)$ (each edge receives a colour from its own list) contains a monochromatic copy of $G$; $R(G,k)$ is the ordinary $k$-colour Ramsey number, obtained when all lists are equal, so $R_\ell(G,k)\le R(G,k)$. The classic probabilistic lower bounds for $R(K_r,2)$ all go through in the list setting, hence $2^{r/2}<R_\ell(K_r,2)\le R(K_r,2)<2^{2r}$, and the authors cannot improve the lower bound. It is not difficult to see that $R_\ell(K_3,2)=6=R(K_3,2)$, but for larger cliques it is open whether the list and ordinary 2-colour Ramsey numbers coincide. In their concluding remarks the authors ask more generally whether $R_\ell(K_r,k)=R(K_r,k)$ for all $r,k$. A conjecture, posted on MathOverflow, that $R_\ell(G,k)=R(G,k)$ always holds is disproved in the paper (for instance for matchings, and for $\ell$-uniform hypergraph cliques with $\ell\ge3$ the list Ramsey number is at most single exponential while the ordinary one grows like a tower).
notes: Stated in prose. The extracted text does not include Section 3 (the paper's dedicated open problems section), so further explicit problems posed there are not captured here.
